timetable = a list of lessons and times for each day
headteacher = the person in charge of a school
form tutor = the teacher responsible for one class
canteen = the room at school where you eat lunch
playground = an outdoor area where students play at break
homework = work teachers give you to do at home
mark = a number or letter that shows how good your work is
fail = to not get the result you need in a test
pass = to succeed in a test or exam
revise = to study again before a test
cheat = to break the rules to get a better result
break time = a short rest between lessons
term = one of the parts of the school year
uniform = special clothes that all students must wear
compulsory = required; you have no choice
optional = you can choose to do it or not
subject = an area of study such as history or English
science = lessons about nature, physics or chemistry
take an exam = to sit a formal test
hand in = to give finished work to the teacher
school trip = a visit organised by the school
locker = a small cupboard at school for your bag and books
whiteboard = a board the teacher writes on with a marker
raise your hand = to put your arm up if you want to speak
detention = time you must stay after school as a punishment
skip classes = to not go to lessons without permission
classmate = a student in the same class as you
staff room = the room where teachers rest and prepare
library = a place with books you can borrow
borrow = to take something for a short time and then return it
primary school = school for younger children
secondary school = school for older children after primary
project = a longer piece of work, often in a group
attend = to go regularly to school or a lesson
concentrate = to give all your attention to something
learn by heart = to memorise something so you can say it without looking
register = the list of students in a class; to mark who is present
absent = not at school
present = at school or in the lesson
late = arriving after the correct time
on time = at the correct time, not late
assembly = a meeting of the whole school, often in the hall
break = a short rest between two lessons
lunch break = the longer midday rest when students eat
after-school club = an activity at school after lessons finish
homework diary = a small book for writing down homework
exercise book = a book of empty pages for writing schoolwork
textbook = the main book used for a subject
workbook = a book of printed exercises
worksheet = a single paper with exercises
folder = a cover for keeping loose papers together
pencil case = a small bag for pens and pencils
rubber = a small object for removing pencil marks
ruler = a straight tool for drawing lines and measuring
highlighter = a bright pen for marking important words
glue stick = a stick of glue for paper
scissors = a tool with two blades for cutting paper
interactive whiteboard = a large computer screen the teacher writes on
computer lab = a room full of computers for lessons
science lab = a room for experiments
gym = a large room for PE
changing rooms = rooms where you change clothes for PE
playing field = a large outdoor grass area for sport
noticeboard = a board where information is pinned up
school office = the room where school secretaries work
headmaster = a man in charge of a school
headmistress = a woman in charge of a school
deputy head = the second person in charge of a school
caretaker = the person who looks after the school building
year group = all the students of the same school year
mixed ability = a class with stronger and weaker students together
set = a class grouped by how good students are at a subject
core subject = a main subject such as maths, English or science
foreign language = a language that is not your first language
art = the school subject of drawing and painting
music = the school subject of singing and instruments
history = the school subject about the past
geography = the school subject about the Earth, countries and maps
biology = the science of living things
chemistry = the science of substances and reactions
physics = the science of energy, forces and motion
ICT = lessons about computers and technology
citizenship = lessons about rights, rules and life in society
tutor group = the class that meets with one tutor for registration
lesson = a period of teaching, usually 45 minutes
period = one numbered slot in the school day
bell = the sound that starts and ends lessons
corridor = a long passage between classrooms
classroom = a room where a class has lessons
sit an exam = to take a formal test
oral exam = a test where you speak, not write
written exam = a test you complete on paper or a computer
mock exam = a practice exam before the real one
pass mark = the lowest result you need to succeed
grade = a letter or word that shows the quality of work
report = a document for parents about a student's work and behaviour
parents' evening = a meeting when teachers talk to parents
coursework = work done during the year that counts towards a grade
deadline = the last day or time you can hand work in
extension = extra time to finish work
cheat sheet = hidden notes used to cheat in a test
revise notes = to study your written notes again
memorise = to learn so you can remember without looking
make mistakes = to get things wrong while you learn
pay attention = to listen and watch carefully
take notes = to write down the important points
hand out = to give papers to everyone in the class
collect in = to take completed work from students
copy from the board = to write down what the teacher wrote on the board
work in pairs = to do a task with one other student
group work = a task done by several students together
presentation = a short talk to the class, often with slides
school rules = the official list of what students may and may not do
exclusion = being sent home or removed from school for serious misbehaviour
uniform policy = the rules about what students must wear
packed lunch = food brought from home to eat at school
school dinner = a hot meal served at school
bus pass = a card that lets you travel to school by bus
open day = a day when visitors can look around the school
graduation = the ceremony at the end of school
